newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Attorney General says HK needs press freedom.
newsitem.headline: Attorney General says HK needs press freedom.

text.p: - Hong Kong's outgoing Attorney General, Jeremy Mathews, laid down a marker on Thursday for Chinese authorities not to interfere with freedom of the press when they take over the British colony.
In a farewell news conference before he steps down in 12 days' time, Mathews said freedom of the press was essential for the rule of law in Hong Kong.
He said the media's right to cover court cases and the actions of judges was a freedom that must not be lost.
"Press freedom is an integral part of the rule of law," Mathews said. "I hope and expect that will continue."

There has been concern that, when Beijing takes over Hong Kong on July 1, there may be rollbacks in judicial and press rights to bring them more into line with the more tightly controlled conditions in the rest of China.
Mathews, praising Hong Kong as an orderly law-abiding society, said there should be no need for China to change laws already in force.
"This (Hong Kong) is a very peaceful and moderate community," he said.
